reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Election and multi-term service of council officers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 3 through A.L. 2015 H.B. 92). Covers election of chairman and vice chairman from council members and permissive eligibility to serve more than a one-year term if elected by council members.

headings.title: State geologist administration and chapter enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 1 by assigning the state geologist to act as council administrator with responsibility for enforcing chapter 259.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of both subsections and history note (through A.L. 2015 H.B. 92), and verified all fingerprints. Checked council officer election, permissive multi-term service, and the state geologist's administrator and chapter-enforcement role. Confirmed both drafted titles accurate and retained them.

headings.title: Oil and Gas Resources Fund creation, revenues, and administration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2015 H.B. 92). Covers creation of the Oil and Gas Resources Fund in the state treasury, enumerated revenue sources including section 259.080 permit application fees and operating, closure, late, and severance fees, and DNR administration. Independent review revised title to include DNR administration alongside fund creation and enumerated revenue sources.

headings.title: Treasurer custody, disbursements, nonreversion, and investments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers state treasurer custody, disbursement approval under sections 30.170 and 30.180, biennial nonreversion to general revenue notwithstanding section 33.080, and investment and interest crediting.

headings.title: Appropriated fund uses for administration and resource data
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers post-appropriation expenditure by DNR exclusively to administer chapter 259 and to collect, process, manage, interpret, and distribute oil-and-gas geologic and hydrologic resource information.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of all three subsections and history note (L. 2015 H.B. 92), and verified all fingerprints. Checked Oil and Gas Resources Fund creation, section 259.080 fee and other deposits, DNR administration, state treasurer custody and sections 30.170/30.180 disbursements, section 33.080 nonreversion, investment crediting, and exclusive post-appropriation uses. Revised subsection 1 to include DNR administration; retained subsections 2 and 3.

headings.title: Chapter administration and council meeting schedule
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 7 through A.L. 2015 H.B. 92). Covers the council's duty to administer chapter 259 and requirement to meet at least once each calendar quarter and on call of the chairperson.

headings.title: Biennial review of chapter statutes and rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers the council's biennial review of chapter 259 statutes and rules, recommending statutory changes if necessary and amending rules accordingly.

headings.title: Advisory committee formation, membership, and recommendations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and history note. Covers the council's power and duty to form an advisory committee for subsection 2 statutory/rule reviews and pre-review of proposed changes, its composition (department, industry, and council members), pre-quarterly meetings, council-designated chair, and permissive fee/funding recommendations.

headings.title: Investigations of waste and facts justifying action
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 5(8) inspections by covering the council's general duty and authority, acting through DNR, to conduct investigations deemed proper to determine whether waste exists or is imminent or other facts justify action. Independent review revised title to capture both existing/imminent waste inquiries and investigations of other facts justifying action.

headings.title: Regulatory orders, rulemaking, well plugging, inspections, and conversions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 including subdivisions (1)(a)–(i), (2)(a)–(f), and (3)–(9) and history note. Covers the council's enumerated authorities acting through DNR: issuing compliance orders (ownership, logs/cores, casing/plugging, surety/personal bonds, hydrocarbon measurement, ratios, clearance certificates, metering, records), adopting rules (bond release/forfeiture, drilling/plugging, treatment, spacing, enhanced recovery, waste disposal), allocating production, classifying wells, contracting/entering land with consent or injunctive relief to plug/remediate abandoned wells (with police-power, non-liability, and crop-timing provisions), warrant-backed inspections, and landowner water-well conversion feasibility with operator release and landowner expense.

headings.title: Rulemaking effectiveness under section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Conditions effectiveness of any chapter 259 rule or portion of a rule on promulgation pursuant to section 536.024.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of all six subsections (including all subdivisions and paragraphs in subsections 3 and 5) and history note (through A.L. 2015 H.B. 92), and verified all fingerprints. Checked quarterly meeting and biennial review duties, advisory committee structure, waste/other-facts investigations, comprehensive regulatory/bonding/plugging/inspection/water-well-conversion authorities, and section 536.024 rulemaking effectiveness. Revised subsection 4 to cover both waste and other facts justifying action; retained subsections 1–3, 5, and 6.

headings.title: Notice and permit requirements for drilling, deepening, or injection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 8 through A.L. 2023 S.B. 109). Covers the prohibition on commencing oil/gas well drilling, deepening to a different formation, or enhanced-recovery/disposal injection without prior notice to and a permit from the state geologist under council rules.

headings.title: Fee review, rulemaking, legislative disapproval, and 2031 revision sunset
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers DNR's permissive fee-structure review with stakeholder input, two-thirds council approval, rulemaking filing under sections 536.021 and 536.024 by December 1, general assembly 60-day concurrent-resolution disapproval, January 1 effective date, expiration of council fee-revision authority on August 28, 2031, and continuation of existing fees upon expiration. Independent review revised title to clarify that the August 28, 2031 sunset expires council fee-revision authority while existing fees remain in place.

headings.title: Late fees, administrative payment orders, and collection suits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers late fees for unpaid fees or overdue reports/forms/information, DNR administrative payment orders, and attorney general collection actions (including interest, attorney's fees, and costs) in Cole County or the well's county.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of all three subsections and history note (through A.L. 2023 S.B. 109), and verified all fingerprints. Checked drilling/deepening/injection permit prerequisites, stakeholder fee review, two-thirds council approval, December 1 rulemaking under sections 536.021/536.024, 60-day legislative concurrent-resolution disapproval, August 28, 2031 sunset of council fee-revision authority (with existing fees remaining in place), and late-fee/administrative-order/AG-collection remedies. Revised subsection 2 to clarify that the 2031 sunset applies to fee-revision authority; retained subsections 1 and 3.

headings.title: Pool spacing units, location exceptions, modifications, and appeals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (4) and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 10 through A.L. 2015 H.B. 92). Covers council spacing units and zones to prevent waste or protect correlative rights, efficient size/shape standards, department exception locations with equitable-share safeguards, modification of pool orders by DNR/state geologist, and 30-day appeal of DNR orders to the council.

headings.title: Noncommercial gas well bonds, drilling units, and variances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers bond filing under section 259.070(5)(1)(d), drilling unit setback (165 feet) and maximum depth (800 feet) conditions, and permissive variance applications to DNR for noncommercial gas wells.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of both subsections (including subdivisions (1)–(4) of subsection 1) and history note (through A.L. 2015 H.B. 92), and verified all fingerprints. Checked pool spacing units and zones, location exceptions with equitable-share safeguards, DNR/state geologist modifications, 30-day council appeal, and noncommercial gas well section 259.070(5)(1)(d) bond, 165-foot setback/800-foot depth limits, and variance applications. Confirmed both drafted titles accurate and retained them.

headings.title: Voluntary pooling and compulsory pooling orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 11). Covers voluntary pooling by owners and royalty owners within a spacing unit, compulsory council pooling orders upon application after notice and hearing on just and reasonable terms, and deeming unit drilling operations and allocated production as occurring on each separately owned tract.

headings.title: Drilling and operating costs, disputes, and production liens
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers pooling-order provisions for reasonable actual drilling/operating costs and supervision charges, council resolution of cost disputes, operator liens on non-paying owners' production shares upon complying with section 259.130, and marketing/sale of liened oil and gas as provided in section 259.100 (retaining both statutory cross-references as written). Independent review revised title to cover both drilling and operating costs alongside supervision charges, disputes, section 259.130 liens, and section 259.100 marketing/sale cross-reference.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of both subsections and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 11), and verified all fingerprints. Checked voluntary and compulsory spacing-unit pooling, tract attribution of operations and production, cost sharing and supervision charges, council cost-dispute authority, and operator liens citing sections 259.130 and 259.100 (both cross-references retained as written). Revised subsection 2 to include operating alongside drilling costs; retained subsection 1.

headings.title: Voluntary unit agreements, approval, and antitrust exemption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 12, A.L. 1972 S.B. 431, H.B. 1176). Covers authorization of voluntary unit or cooperative field/pool agreements, state antitrust exemption conditioned on council approval under public-interest/correlative-rights/recovery criteria, and limitation of binding effect to executing parties and their successors.

headings.title: Petitions and hearings for compulsory unit operation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and history note. Covers filing a petition by executing owners when one or more interest owners refuse to execute a unit plan, council notice and public hearing, and required petition contents (unit area description, operation nature, conformed agreements).

headings.title: Required findings and binding effect of unitization orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and history note. Covers mandatory council findings—75% record legal title approval of drilling/producing rights and 75% of royalty/production payments, reasonable necessity, and recovered value exceeding additional cost—triggering a unit operation order binding on all interest owners.

headings.title: Required terms of compulsory unit operation orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1) through (6) and history note. Covers the fair-and-reasonable standard and six required elements of a unit operation order: unit area description, fair production allocation, investment credits and charges, proportional expense sharing, unit operator and commencement time, and non-conflicting additional provisions.

headings.title: Several liability and cap on owner unit expenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Establishes that each tract owner's liability for unit expenses is several rather than joint or collective and capped at the amount apportioned or charged to that owner's interest under the unitization plan.

headings.title: Enlarging existing unit areas and preserving tract factors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Covers council authority after petition, notice, and hearing to enlarge a previously ordered unit area, agreement execution thresholds (including the proviso where existing agreements allow additions), treating the prior unit area as a single tract for allocation, and barring alteration of prior relative tract factors without consent of all affected tract owners.

headings.title: Effect and required terms of unit enlargement orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Applies subsection 3 binding effect, subsection 4 required provisions, and subsections 5 and 6 obligation rules to council orders entered under subsection 6 for enlarged unit areas.

headings.title: Attribution of unit production and operations to tracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Deems allocated unit production and council-ordered unit operations on any part of the unit area to be actual production and operations on each separately owned tract for all purposes.

headings.title: State antitrust exemption for council-ordered unit operations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 1 by stating that unit formation and operation under council order pursuant to subsections 2 through 9 do not violate state trust, monopoly, or restraint-of-trade statutes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of all nine subsections (including subdivisions in subsections 2–4) and history note (through A.L. 1972 S.B. 431, H.B. 1176), and verified all fingerprints. Checked voluntary unit agreements and conditional antitrust exemption, compulsory unitization petitions, 75% title/royalty findings, mandatory order terms, several liability cap, unit enlargement and tract-factor preservation, tract attribution, and subsection 9 antitrust exemption for council-ordered units. Confirmed all nine drafted titles accurate and distinct, and retained them.

headings.title: Council practice and procedure rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 14). Directs the council to prescribe rules and regulations governing practice and procedure before it.

headings.title: Hearing and ten-day notice for nonemergency orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Prohibits council orders or amendments without a public hearing on at least ten days' notice, except in emergencies, and guarantees interested persons the right to be heard. Independent review revised title to preserve the express emergency exception distinguishing subsection 2 from subsection 3.

headings.title: Emergency orders without notice and fifteen-day limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 2 by authorizing immediate emergency orders without hearing notice when an emergency requiring immediate action is found, with a maximum fifteen-day duration.

headings.title: Methods, publication, contents, and service of notices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers council election between personal service or letter plus county newspaper publication (or Jefferson City publication for statewide notices), required notice contents and state geologist signature, personal-service officers or agents, and proof of agent service by affidavit.

headings.title: Written orders, public records, and certified copies as evidence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires council orders to be written, entered in full, indexed by the state geologist, and open for public inspection during reasonable office hours, and makes certified copies of rules, regulations, or orders admissible as originals in state courts.

headings.title: Initiating proceedings, hearing scheduling, and order deadlines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Covers action on the council's own motion or an interested person's petition, prompt hearing scheduling without undue delay, and 30-day order deadlines after hearing or after submission of a finding of facts.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of all six subsections and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 14), and verified all fingerprints. Checked council procedure rules, ten-day hearing notice with express emergency exception, fifteen-day emergency orders, personal/letter/newspaper/Jefferson City notice methods, written indexed public orders and certified evidentiary copies, and 30-day order entry deadlines. Revised subsection 2 to preserve the emergency exception; retained subsections 1 and 3–6.

headings.title: Submitting contested fact questions to Public Service Commission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 15). Requires submission to the Public Service Commission for hearing whenever either party to a contested matter avers a question or questions of fact.

headings.title: Public Service Commission hearing rules and regulations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Applies Public Service Commission practice rules and regulations to fact-finding hearings conducted under subsection 1.

headings.title: Assessment and taxation of commission hearing costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Grants the Public Service Commission discretion to set and tax costs in the action as it sees fit.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of all three subsections and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 15), and verified all fingerprints. Checked mandatory submission of contested fact questions to the Public Service Commission, application of commission hearing rules, and discretionary cost assessment/taxation. Confirmed all three drafted titles accurate and retained them.

headings.title: Circuit court appeals, venue, notice, and transcripts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 17). Covers appeal by an adversely affected person to Cole County or affected-property county circuit court, 30-day notice-of-appeal filing and required contents, appellant-paid hearing transcript, and 60-day transcript delivery. Independent review revised title to name circuit court appeals neutrally without overstating an unconditional right.

headings.title: Filing transcript, review petition, and dismissal rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers 90-day circuit court filing of transcript and petition for review, perfecting appeal via timely notice, and permissive dismissal for late filing unless extended by the court for good cause. Independent review revised punctuation for clarity while retaining 90-day filing, appeal perfection, and permissive good-cause-qualified dismissal rules.

headings.title: Suspending appealed orders and supersedeas bond requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers applying to suspend an appealed council order, council fixing bond amount, 10-day filing and approval of supersedeas bond running in favor of the state for damaged persons, and continued operation of unsuspended orders during appeal.

headings.title: Court precedence, transcript review, and standard of review
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers circuit court docket precedence insofar as practicable, review on the council transcript, judgment affirming or reversing, and sustaining council orders when regularly pursued and supported by law and substantial, credible evidence.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of all four subsections and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 17), and verified all fingerprints. Checked Cole County or property-county circuit court venue, 30-day appeal notice, appellant-paid 60-day transcript, 90-day circuit court filing and good-cause-qualified dismissal, 10-day supersedeas bond suspension, docket precedence, and substantial/credible-evidence review standard. Revised subsections 1 and 2 for neutrality and punctuation clarity; retained subsections 3 and 4.

headings.title: Contraband declaration, in rem seizure actions, and intervention
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 19, A.L. 1983 H.B. 37, A.L. 2015 H.B. 92). Declares illegal oil, gas, and products contraband subject to cumulative seizure and sale, authorizes standalone or joined in rem actions by the attorney general in the county where found, and grants interest claimants a right to intervene.

headings.title: In rem procedure, service, default bar, and seizure orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers strictly in rem action without plaintiff bond, attorney general notice and civil-action service with affidavit, 30-day appearance bar, immediate court seizure order directing sheriff custody, and optional delivery to a bonded court-appointed agent.

headings.title: Claimant bond to release seized oil, gas, or product
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Allows a contesting interest claimant to obtain pre-sale release of seized oil, gas, or product by furnishing a court-approved bond to the sheriff equal to 150% of market value conditioned on redelivery or payment and court compliance.

headings.title: Sheriff's sale of contraband and purchaser title
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers court-ordered sheriff's sale after hearing (following civil execution sale rules, with optional lot or interval sales), vesting of title free of prior claims, and conversion to legal oil, gas, or product in the purchaser's hands.

headings.title: Oil and Gas Remedial Fund, deposits, custody, and uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Credits net contraband sale proceeds and section 259.070(5)(1)(d) bond forfeitures to the newly created Oil and Gas Remedial Fund for DNR well plugging or remedial measures, with state treasurer custody, sections 30.170 and 30.180 disbursements, nonreversion notwithstanding section 33.080, and investment/interest crediting.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of all five subsections and history note (through A.L. 2015 H.B. 92), and verified all fingerprints. Checked contraband declaration, cumulative in rem AG seizure suits and intervention, strictly in rem procedure with 30-day default bar, 150%-value claimant release bond, sheriff's execution sale vesting clear legal title, and Oil and Gas Remedial Fund creation (including section 259.070(5)(1)(d) bond forfeitures, sections 30.170/30.180 disbursements, and section 33.080 nonreversion). Confirmed all five drafted titles accurate and retained them.

headings.title: Per-day penalties and exclusive-penalty exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 20). Sets a penalty of not more than $1,000 per violation act and per continuing day for violating chapter 259 or council rules, regulations, or orders, unless chapter 259 specifically provides an exclusive penalty. Independent review removed unstated "civil" qualifier because subsection 1 refers simply to a monetary penalty (recovered by attorney general suit under subsection 4).

headings.title: Misdemeanor for evasive false reports or record tampering
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Makes evasive false entries or statements in required reports or records, willful omissions, or removal from the state, destruction, mutilation, alteration, or falsification of required records a misdemeanor punishable as provided by law. Independent review revised title to preserve the statutory evasion purpose and cover omissions, removal from the state, destruction, mutilation, alteration, and falsification.

headings.title: Penalties for knowingly aiding or abetting violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Subjects any person knowingly aiding or abetting another in violating chapter 259 or council rules, regulations, or orders to the same chapter penalty as the underlying violation.

headings.title: Attorney general penalty suits, venue, and preserved liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers attorney general suits on the council's behalf to recover section penalties in defendant's residence or violation county, and specifies that penalty payment neither legalizes illegal oil, gas, or products nor relieves private damages liability.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of all four subsections and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 20), and verified all fingerprints. Checked $1,000 per-act/per-day penalty with exclusive-penalty exception, evasive false report/record misdemeanor, knowing aiding-and-abetting liability, and AG penalty suits preserving illegality and private damages liability. Revised subsections 1 and 2 to avoid adding "civil" and to capture evasion/omission/tampering scope; retained subsections 3 and 4.

headings.title: Attorney general injunction suits and contraband impoundment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 2d Ex. Sess. p. 917 § 21, A.L. 2015 H.B. 92). Covers council or DNR requests for attorney general suits to restrain actual or threatened chapter/rule/order violations in circuit court, court jurisdiction to grant prohibitory and mandatory injunctions without bond, and restraining or impounding illegal oil, gas, or products.

headings.title: Injunction suits by affected persons after council inaction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 1 by authorizing an adversely affected person to sue in their own behalf if the council fails to sue within ten days of written request, requiring the council to be joined as a defendant and permitting injunctive relief without bond. Independent review revised "Private injunction suits" to "Injunction suits by affected persons" because the statute authorizes any adversely affected person after a ten-day unanswered written request.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of both subsections and history note (through A.L. 2015 H.B. 92), and verified all fingerprints. Checked council/DNR-requested AG injunction suits without bond including contraband impoundment, and adversely affected persons' injunction suits after ten-day council inaction following written request (with council joined as defendant). Revised subsection 2 from "Private injunction suits" to "Injunction suits by affected persons"; retained subsection 1.
